findings.description: The fix for the r3 blocker introduced a new one of the same species. V-1 now offers two inter-case disciplines as equivalent -- 'Build a fresh one per case, or hard-reset and `git clean -xdff` between cases' -- and they are not equivalent. Neither `git reset --hard` nor `git clean -xdff` touches anything under `.git/`, so the `.git/rebase-merge` and `.git/rebase-apply` directories the B and C cases install by `mkdir` survive into every later case. Running the table in its stated order, cases D1 and D2 -- the merge cases -- arrive carrying both rebase markers. Three consequences, all measured against a CORRECT guard under an otherwise fully B-4-compliant harness. (1) D1 and D2 report the rebase state, so V-2's 'D1 and D2 match a merge-specific string' and its 'each of the three strings fails to match the other two families' cases' both fail correct work, on a blocker clause. (2) V-1's own merge-detector mutation fails correct work: with the merge check deleted, D1 and D2 are required to 'flip to exit 0 or a created commit' and they do not flip, because the surviving rebase markers still refuse them -- V-1 reports a working merge detector as dead, which is verbatim the failure mode revision 2 wrote the attached-HEAD matrix to prevent. (3) It hides a defect in the other direction: a guard with no merge detector at all produces results on D1 and D2 indistinguishable from a guard that has one, so the clause's own promise that 'all three detectors are independently load-bearing' does not hold on this path. Nothing warns the checker, because the new porcelain precondition is satisfied in all nine cases -- `git clean -xdff` does remove the working-tree dirt the clause's stated reason names, so the recipe looks like it worked. The clause's justification is scoped to the dirty marker only, which is exactly why a careful reader concludes the recipe is complete. Fix: delete the alternative, which is what revision 5's own log at :52 already claims the clause does ('V-1 now requires a fresh repo per case'); or, if the shortcut is worth keeping, extend it to `rm -rf .git/rebase-merge .git/rebase-apply .git/MERGE_HEAD` plus a checkout back onto the branch, since a hard reset also leaves HEAD detached after A1 and A2.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline 298c8a6, PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin", $STUBS and $HOME outside the repo, dates pinned through setup, `date` and `osascript` stubbed per B-4, one repo, `git reset --hard; git clean -xdff` between cases exactly as :84 words it. CORRECT guard (inserted after `cd "$SRC"` at :128): A1 markers=[] SAID=DETACHED; B1/B2 markers=[rebase-merge] SAID=REBASE; C1/C2 markers=[rebase-merge rebase-apply] SAID=REBASE; D1 markers=[rebase-merge rebase-apply MERGE_HEAD] SAID=REBASE; D2 same, SAID=REBASE -- V-2 requires MERGE on D1/D2. PRE_PORC empty on A2/B2/C2/D2 and [?? drift.txt] on the five dirty cases in every case, i.e. V-1's precondition passes throughout. Merge-detector mutation (merge block removed, 0 lines matching MERGE_HEAD remaining) under the same recipe: D1 EXIT=1, D2 EXIT=1, neither flips. Same mutation, fresh repo per case: D1 EXIT=0 CNT=1->2, D2 EXIT=0 CNT=1->1, both flip. Isolated mechanism check: with all three markers and an untracked file installed, `git reset --hard && git clean -xdff` leaves MERGE_HEAD gone but rebase-merge PRESENT, rebase-apply PRESENT, HEAD still DETACHED, porcelain []. constitution.md:84 (the alternative), :80 and :94 (the case constructions and the per-detector mutations), :101 (V-2's per-family assertions), :65 ('All three detectors are independently load-bearing'), :52 (the log's 'requires a fresh repo per case').

findings.description: The porcelain precondition states a consequence for only one of the two ways it can be violated. It says the four clean cases 'must show it empty and the five dirty cases must show it non-empty', then gives the void-the-run rule for 'If a clean case shows anything' and nothing for a dirty case showing empty. That second case is reachable and unowned: B-4 requires its two-sided control to run 'before any V-1 case' against the baseline, the positive half runs baseline-on-A1 and commits the dirty marker away, and neither clause says the control gets a repo of its own. Under fresh-repo-per-case the natural reading is that it does, but B-4 was already silent on this when r3 filed it as part of the B-4 major, and revision 5 addressed only the 'any one would close it' framing. It fails safe -- an all-clean A1 makes a defective guard exit 0 and get caught -- so this is a minor, but it is the same shape as the r3 blocker: an observation the checker can make with no rule attached.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:86 (the precondition and its one-sided consequence), :84 (fresh repo per case, scoped to 'each case' of V-1's nine), :168 (B-4's control: 'runs before any V-1 case', no repo-ownership statement). Measured, fresh repos, baseline script: control positive A1 EXIT=0 CNT=1->2 with the marker committed away, leaving porcelain empty; control negative A2 EXIT=0 CNT=1->1, log carries 1 'Nothing to commit' line -- both halves as specified, and the positive half's repo is left clean.

findings.description: Answering the question part 3 was written to settle: yes, an out-of-scope edit inside the allowlisted script can still be purely additive and therefore invisible to the whole document. Two concrete ones, both measured. (a) An added `elif` branch in the push-failure classifier at :169-177 -- two inserted lines, zero removed. D-1's own text forbids it ('The push path at :159-182 is correct as written and is not touched'), and nothing checks it: no clause in the document ever executes the push path, because auto-push is off by default and both of V-4's runs exit at :162. (b) A new phase gated on a tool B-4 requires to be absent, e.g. `if command -v brew ...` writing a Brewfile into $SRC -- five inserted lines, zero removed, no output under the harness, so V-4's streams stay byte-identical while the phase runs for real on the user's machine. Neither is a likely worker move, which is why this is a minor rather than a reopening: part 3 does close the class the r3 escape used, and closing the additive class needs a judgment read ('every added hunk belongs to the guard') that would change D-1's routing from deterministic to judgment. Worth naming in the clause as a known residual rather than leaving the next reader to rediscover it.
findings.evidence: Measured on clones of 298c8a6 with each edit committed. `git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync | grep -c '^-[^-]'`: push-path elif branch -> 0 removed, 2 added; brew-gated phase -> 0 removed, 5 added. Both keep D-1 part 1 at the allowlisted path only. V-4 run for each against the baseline, attached-dirty and attached-clean, merged stream plus exit code, scratch path normalized -> IDENTICAL for both. B-1's pattern matches neither added block. constitution.md:174 (the push-path non-goal), :178 (part 3), :115 (V-4's comparison).

findings.description: `DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH` is the one environment variable that changes which branch the script takes at :159, and B-4's stub contract never names it, despite the clause's own bar that 'every stub is named rather than assumed'. It decides whether the document catches its own D-1 failing example in the additive form. Measured: with the variable unset, an inserted `: "${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:=1}"` is caught by V-4, whose attached-dirty run diverges into '==> Pushing to origin' against the bare origin. With the variable pinned to 0 -- which a checker is quite likely to do, since not wanting a probe to push is the obvious instinct -- the same edit passes V-4 byte-identical and joins the invisible set above. One line in the stub list ('left unset, so the runs exercise the documented default') makes the coverage deterministic instead of dependent on an unstated harness choice.
findings.evidence: Measured, two clones of 298c8a6: baseline vs a clone with `: "${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:=1}"` inserted after `set -euo pipefail` (0 removed lines, 1 added). Attached-dirty, harness otherwise identical. Variable unset: base last line '==> Committed locally. Auto-push is off; push manually: ...', cand last line '==> Done. Other machines can pull with `chezmoi update`.', diff shows '==> Pushing to origin' and 'cb98b60..eae221a main -> main' -- V-4 DIFFERS, caught. Variable exported as 0: V-4 IDENTICAL, invisible. constitution.md:161-168 (the stub list), dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:159.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: revision 5 closes the r3 blocker on the fresh-repo path. The r3 attack, rebuilt from scratch rather than replayed -- a guard identical to a correct one except placed after the clean-tree exit at :130-133, run under a fully B-4-compliant harness -- is caught by the plain `exit != 0` assertion once each case gets its own repo, with no reliance on the porcelain reading at all. The correct guard passes all nine.
findings.evidence: Measured, fresh repo per case, $STUBS and $HOME outside the repo, PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin", date and osascript stubbed. DEFECTIVE guard: A1 EXIT=1, A2 EXIT=0 (VIOLATES exit!=0), B1 EXIT=1, B2 EXIT=0, C1 EXIT=1, C2 EXIT=0, D1 EXIT=1, D2 EXIT=0, E1 EXIT=1 -- all four clean cases caught. CORRECT guard: all nine EXIT=1, commit counts 1->1, staged paths unchanged. PRE_PORC empty on A2/B2/C2/D2 and [?? drift.txt] on the dirty five under both guards. constitution.md:84.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, on the opposite-hole question: the void-the-run reframing does not let a checker dismiss a genuine artifact failure. The precondition is scoped to one datum -- the pre-run porcelain of a clean case -- and under fresh-repo-per-case that datum is measured before the artifact has run, on a repo the harness built moments earlier, so no behaviour of the script can reach it. Measured: the correct and defective guards produce identical PRE_PORC columns across all nine cases, which is precisely the property that makes the reading safe. Everything a defective artifact does show up in is post-run (exit code, commit count, staged paths), and the void rule says nothing about those. Note the dependency, though: this soundness comes from fresh repos. Under the reset alternative the precondition becomes a function of the previous case's run, so the blocker above also reopens this.
findings.evidence: Measured, fresh repo per case. CORRECT guard PRE_PORC: A1 [?? drift.txt], A2 [], B1 [?? drift.txt], B2 [], C1 [?? drift.txt], C2 [], D1 [?? drift.txt], D2 [], E1 [?? drift.txt]. DEFECTIVE guard: byte-identical column. constitution.md:86.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: part 3 catches both r3 escapes, re-derived by committing them fresh rather than trusting the r3 record. It also costs a correct implementation nothing -- a guard inserted after `cd "$SRC"`, with or without a helper, is pure insertion.
findings.evidence: Measured on clones of 298c8a6, each edit committed. `git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync | grep -c '^-[^-]'`: the :137 bare-compound 'fix' (`[[ "$file_count" != "1" ]] && files_word="files"` -> `if [ ... ]; then ...; fi`) -> 1, CATCHES; `${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:-0}` flipped to `:-1` -> 1, CATCHES; both together -> 2, CATCHES. The correct guard used throughout these measurements -> 0. constitution.md:178.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the `date` stub closes the r3 V-4 minor, and it breaks nothing else. `date` has exactly one call site in the script, the commit subject at :142, so no other phase can be affected by pinning it; grepped rather than assumed. With the stub in place V-4's two runs match across a simulated UTC day boundary, including the abbreviated sha the clause forbids normalizing.
findings.evidence: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync at 298c8a6, `grep -n '\bdate\b'` -> only :142 `commit_msg="[auto-sync from ${HOST}] $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) - ..."`. Measured, attached-dirty, dates pinned through setup: stub returning 2026-08-09 for one run and 2026-08-10 for the other -> `[main b3c7a3c] ... 2026-08-09 - 1 file` vs `[main f29169d] ... 2026-08-10 - 1 file`, streams DIFFER (the r3 minor reproduced). Stub returning a single fixed value for both -> `[main eae221a] ... 2026-01-01 - 1 file` on both sides, streams IDENTICAL with only the scratch path normalized. constitution.md:164, :115.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: B-4's full-argument-list osascript stub makes V-3's title assertion checkable, and the title really is the discriminator it is claimed to be. Measured: exactly one recorded call per refusing case, all nine carrying `with title "Dotfiles sync failed"`, and zero calls on the clean attached run -- so the assertion is not trivially satisfiable by any run that touches osascript.
findings.evidence: Measured, correct guard, fresh repo per case, stub appending "$*" to a record file outside the repo. A1..E1: osascript_calls=1, title='with title "Dotfiles sync failed"' in all nine. Clean attached run: osascript_calls=0. constitution.md:163 (the stub contract), :108 (V-3's assertion), dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:28-31 vs :33-36.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: both r3 minors on this clause are closed in the text. The four required committed cases may now 'live in one new file or several', which removes the singular-file assumption, and any merge case must be built with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD`, which aligns the worker's construction with V-1's probe so the two cannot encode different contracts.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:151. Underlying premise re-measured: the unguarded baseline exits 0 on all nine blocked-state cases and on both attached cases, so every blocked-state case has something to flip and no per-detector mutation touches the attached path.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: every external fact the document leans on, re-derived from the artifacts at 298c8a6 rather than carried forward from r3. The baseline commit is also the repo's current HEAD with a clean tree, so `298c8a6..HEAD` is empty today and D-1 and D-2's diff-scoped checks start from zero rather than from unrelated drift -- worth stating because both clauses would silently inherit any commits that landed in between.
findings.evidence: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> 298c8a6; `git rev-list --count 298c8a6..HEAD` -> 0; `git status --porcelain` -> empty. Script is 182 lines; :16 `set -euo pipefail`, :26 the tee redirect, :28-31 notify, :33-36 notify_fail, :128 `cd "$SRC"`, :130-133 the clean-tree exit, :142 the commit subject, :153-158 the push rationale, :159-182 the push path. Bare compounds at exactly :88, :122, :137. Floors by `/usr/bin/grep -c '^@test'`: apps 18, doctor 11, font 44, install-failures 17, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, lint 1, packages 13; `bats --count tests/` = 120, so D-2's '>120' is a real floor. B-1's fenced pattern compared programmatically against tests/lint.bats:50 -> byte-identical, True; lint.bats's guarded surface is `$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/*.bats` plus helpers.bash plus mutation-check.sh, which excludes the sync script and includes any new tests/*.bats file, exactly as the note at :59 says.

findings.description: Cold read, as a worker with no audit history: the document is followable and the work it describes is unambiguous. Two things such a worker would still get wrong that no clause catches, neither worth a severity. First, the one r3 raised and revision 5 did not fold in: because the guard sits after `chezmoi re-add` at :66, a refusal leaves the source dir dirtier than it found it -- the capture phases have already written $HOME's changes in. That is correct under Phase 0 override 1 and under the spec's 'before staging anything', but a reader infers the opposite from 'refuses before staging', and on the incident's machine it means every refused daily run accumulates uncommitted captures. One sentence in V-1's placement paragraph would close it. Second, commit ordering: D-3 requires each commit to be green at checkout, so a worker who commits the tests before the guard ships a red commit. D-3's check does catch that, so it costs a rework round rather than an escape, but the constraint is only derivable, never stated.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:9 (override 1), :90 (the placement paragraph), :191-192 (D-3). dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:64-69 (`chezmoi re-add`, unguarded, before :128). Measured: every refusing case reaches '==> Capturing live $HOME changes back into source' before printing its refusal.
